"executive_summary": "The NCI's Clinical Proteomics Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) has generated comprehensive proteogenomic profiles for multiple cancer types, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). While these data reveal regulatory relationships between proteins and posttranscriptional modifications, the resulting co-expression networks are too large and complex for effective static visualization. To address this, the authors developed ProNetView-ccRCC, an interactive web-based portal that enables intuitive 3D exploration of the ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network. The network comprises 3,614 genes and 30 functional pathway-enriched modules derived from 20,976 phosphopeptides across 103 samples. The tool utilizes the Three.js framework and iCAVE layout algorithms to render the network in 3D, allowing users to rotate, zoom, and filter data based on clinical variables such as tumor grade, stage, age, and gender. Users can query specific genes, such as ERG, to view their connections and associations with phenotypes, or explore module-specific pathway enrichments. summary.title: ProNetView-ccRCC: A web-based portal to interactively explore clear cell renal cell carcinoma proteogenomics networks
summary.authors: Selim Kalayci; Francesca Petralia; Pei Wang; Zeynep H Gümüş
summary.executive_summary: The National Cancer Institute's Clinical Proteomics Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) has generated extensive proteogenomic data for various cancers, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). While these data reveal complex gene/protein regulatory networks, visualizing and navigating such high-dimensional structures remains a significant challenge for researchers. Existing tools often rely on static 2D images or lack the interactivity required for deep exploration of network topologies and associated metadata. To address this gap, the authors developed ProNetView-ccRCC, an open-access, web-based interactive portal. This tool utilizes a 3D network exploration interface built on the Three.js framework to allow users to intuitively navigate the ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network, which comprises 3,614 genes and 30 functional pathway-enriched modules. Users can query specific genes, such as the oncogene ERG, to visualize their connections and associations with clinical variables like tumor grade. The portal also facilitates the exploration of network modules and their enriched pathways, providing a centralized resource for hypothesis generation and data communication without requiring plugin installation. By integrating phosphoproteomics data from 103 ccRCC samples with clinical metadata, ProNetView-ccRCC serves as a critical community resource for interpreting the molecular mechanisms driving ccRCC progression.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
The National Cancer Institute's Clinical Proteomics Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) has generated extensive proteogenomic data for various cancers, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). While these data reveal complex gene/protein regulatory networks, visualizing and navigating such high-dimensional structures remains a significant challenge for researchers. Existing tools often rely on static 2D images or lack the interactivity required for deep exploration of network topologies and associated metadata. To address this gap, the authors developed ProNetView-ccRCC, an open-access, web-based interactive portal. This tool utilizes a 3D network exploration interface built on the Three.js framework to allow users to intuitively navigate the ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network, which comprises 3,614 genes and 30 functional pathway-enriched modules. Users can query specific genes, such as the oncogene ERG, to visualize their connections and associations with clinical variables like tumor grade. The portal also facilitates the exploration of network modules and their enriched pathways, providing a centralized resource for hypothesis generation and data communication without requiring plugin installation. By integrating phosphoproteomics data from 103 ccRCC samples with clinical metadata, ProNetView-ccRCC serves as a critical community resource for interpreting the molecular mechanisms driving ccRCC progression.

Research Context
Large-scale proteogenomic studies have advanced cancer understanding. Co-expression networks reveal regulatory relationships between proteins. Visualizing complex network models remains a significant challenge. Current tools often lack interactivity for user-initiated exploration. A centralized platform customized for CPTAC data is necessary.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can an interactive web portal improve the exploration of ccRCC networks? Does a 3D interface facilitate better navigation of dense network topologies? Can users effectively query associations between phosphopeptides and clinical variables? Will integrating pathway metadata enhance the interpretation of network modules? Is a plugin-free web solution accessible to researchers with varying skills?

Methodological Details
The study focuses on clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Data was derived from 103 ccRCC tumor samples. The network characterizes 20,976 phosphopeptides. Network construction used a random-forest based algorithm. Two genes connect if at least two phosphopeptides map to them. 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules were identified. Modules were derived using the Glay clustering algorithm. Modules containing at least 20 genes were selected. Pathway enrichment was performed via Fisher Exact test. The portal is hosted at http://ccrcc.cptac-network-view.org/.

Procedures And Architectures
The portal enables interactive explorations in 3D. Implementation builds on the Three.js framework. Three.js provides an interface for WebGL. Network layouts were calculated using 3D algorithms within iCAVE. iCAVE is a desktop-based tool for stereoscopic exploration. Client-side Javascript libraries handle user interaction events. Libraries include D3.js, dataTables.js, and JQuery. Styling utilized Bootstrap v3.3.7. The portal runs without additional plug-ins. Users can rotate and zoom in/out the 3D view.

Key Results
The network comprises 3,614 genes. The network includes 30 functional pathway-enriched modules. Six modules were significantly associated with biological pathways. Querying ERG returned a p-value of 0.003 for tumor grade. Querying ERG returned an FDR of 0.118 for tumor grade. ERG is directly connected to 11 genes within the same module. ERG maps to 5 different peptides. Users can specify an FDR cutoff value of 20%. Pathways are sorted by their p-values. The tool runs on any modern web browser.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The tool facilitates hypothesis generation for future studies. It helps understand the phosphopeptide network in context. The portal aids in identifying central genes via node sizes. It allows visualization of gene locations and connections. The resource supports researchers with a wide-spectrum of skills. It enables sharing and communication of results.

Claims
ProNetView-ccRCC provides an intuitive environment for exploring ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression networks. Users can interactively explore the large and dense topology of the whole ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network in 3D by rotating and zooming in/out the view. Its 3D network exploration interface enables quick and easy interactions with the ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network as well as 30 functional network modules and their associated meta-data. Users can easily query for genes of their interest in the network.  Overall, these help understand the phosphopeptide network in the context of markers of user interest to help guide hypothesis generation for future studies.
The portal effectively integrates network topology with clinical metadata. Users can interact with the network portal and can conveniently query for association between abundance of each phosphopeptide in the network and clinical variables such as tumor grade. To query whether other genes have similar association to tumor grade as ERG, users can easily construct a simple query for those genes (Figure 2C ) by specifying the phenotype of interest (grade) and the FDR cutoff value (FDR= 20%).  Overall, these help understand the phosphopeptide network in the context of markers of user interest to help guide hypothesis generation for future studies.

Data And Code Availability
The portal is an open-access freely available resource. The tool runs on all modern web browsers.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1A displays the global ccRCC tumor phosphoproteomics co-expression network. Figure 1B links the network to functional network modules. Figure 1C shows the query results for the oncogene ERG. Figure 2A displays a snapshot of the Angiogenesis enriched module network. Figure 2B shows the gene-level meta-data panel. Figure 3A displays the interactive table listing enriched pathways.

Three Takeaways
1. ProNetView-ccRCC is an open-access portal for ccRCC network exploration. 2. The 3D interface allows intuitive interaction with 3,614 genes. 3. The tool facilitates hypothesis generation without plugins.
